title: Recipe Chips — compact multi-step assistant blocks (scratchpad)
content:
Problem statement:
- Users often need a short, repeatable multi-step interaction (e.g., data-cleanup steps, interview prep checklist, short tutorial) that feels like a single compact widget inside a chat.
- Current sessions blow tokens for small repeated steps and UX doesn’t surface step progress or allow reusing a saved micro-flow.

Idea (working name: Recipe Chips):
- Compact, card-like flow that contains 3–7 ordered steps. Each step can be a prompt template + optional tool call or structured input.
- Chips are embeddable into a chat message or persisted as a session-scope template. Lightweight state stored as step index + minimal slot values (prefilled answers).
- Goal: reduce token cost by avoiding full prompt regen for repeated micro-flows; increase repeatability and discoverability of common tasks.

Core user stories:
- As an end user, I can run a saved "recipe chip" (e.g., "bug triage checklist") and progress through steps without typing.
- As a product engineer, I can programmatically create recipe chips via the API and bind them to a route/recommendation.
- As an admin, I can version chips and roll out an updated step to 10% of users for feedback.

Behavioral sketches / UX notes:
- Inline: small pill with title, badge (3 steps) and CTA "Run".
- Runner overlay: shows step content, minimal input fields, prev/next buttons, progress bar. Compact view shows summary only and defers LLM generation until step needed.
- Completed run returns a concise structured summary (JSON + short natural language recap) that can be stored as a conversation artifact.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create / run a recipe chip via Console and API.
- Step navigation (prev/next), basic input binding to steps.
- Outputs: per-step LLM response, final consolidated summary.
- Metric events emitted: chip_run_start, chip_step_submit, chip_run_complete, chip_run_abort.

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /v1/chips {name, steps: [{type: "prompt"|"tool", template, slots}], visibility: "user"|"org"|"public", version}
- POST /v1/chips/{id}/run {session_id, prefill: {slot: value}} -> returns run_id, first_step_payload
- PATCH /v1/chips/{id}/run/{run_id}/step {step_index, slot_values} -> returns step_result

Token/cost strategy:
- Keep templates server-side; only send minimal slot values + step_id + run_id to LLM for step generation.
- Use prefix caching for repeated runs of the same chip template.
- Allow a compact-mode that uses a smaller model for intermediate steps and a higher-fidelity model for final summary.

Telemetry / logging (events & suggested attributes):
- chip_run_start: chip_id, user_id, entry_point (ui|api|recommendation), template_version
- chip_step_submit: chip_id, run_id, step_index, model_hint, tokens_in, tokens_out
- chip_run_complete: chip_id, run_id, total_steps, duration_ms, final_model, success=true/false

Rollout / experiment ideas:
- Canary versioning: chip versions and rollouts by user cohort (10% auto, 50% after 2 days).
- Cost experiment: default intermediate steps on small model for 90% of runs, measure final-summary quality delta.
- Discovery experiment: expose chips as suggestions in completion UI vs. pinned chips in Console; compare activation rate and downstream retention.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Storage: keep full step transcripts in conversation history? (privacy + token cost). Maybe only store final summary and pointers to step metadata.
- Offline playback: should chips be exportable JSON so customer infra (Private) can run them locally? (likely yes)
- Slot typing and validation: will we invent a QL for slot constraints or reuse existing structured output schema?
- Failure modes: step tool call fails / model hallucination — need to show retry, skip, or escalate to human.

Implementation notes / infra concerns:
- Runner should be low-latency; consider a special route that pins warm kernels for chips with known short sequences.
- Prefetching: pre-warm KV cache for chip template when a user views many chips (heuristic).
- RBAC: chips visible at user/org/public scopes; Console must show ownership and allow cloning.

Quick TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Proto: define minimal chip schema and run API sketch -> add to ux-protos repo (assign: Nadia)
- [ ] Experiment plan: 2-week canary with 50 power users in hosted beta (assign: Ethan)
- [ ] UX mockups: compact pill, runner overlay low-fi (assign: Lena)
- [ ] Telemetry spec: event names + attributes -> add to events spreadsheet (assign: Mika)

Notes to self:
- Keep MVP small: no embedded tool orchestration (only basic tool-call step)
- Lean on existing rollout infra (console + rollouts) to avoid shipping new gating primitives
- Finish proto before end of month to get engineering cycle in Q1 planning

Random brainstorm fragments (ignore / keep):
- Could chain chips: output of chip A can populate chip B slots (workflow chest).
- Chip marketplace for teams (shareable templates) with vetting and usage badges.
- Quick keyboard shortcut: /chip <name> to insert into chat and run with defaults.
- Possible alternative name: "mini-recipes", "task-sprints", "flow-snippets" — "recipe chips" is playful and suggests compactness.

End of scratchpad.
